_readme: Club identity and static text. Edit this file (or point fetchers at a published Google Sheet) — no code changes needed.
_demo: true turns on the banner saying everything on screen is invented. Set it to false in the same edit that replaces the demo content in schedule.json, results.json and status.json — never before.
tagline: Replace this with one line about the club.
_features: Which parts of the app are live. Phase 1 is the static content only: club intro, photos, schedule, contacts. Turn each of these on when that phase's content is real — not when its code is written. A status panel nobody updates and an example yardage both teach players to distrust the app. 'yardage' and 'results' also take "preview": the tab appears and describes the feature, with no data behind it.
_scorecard: The scorecard needs no content, so it can be on from day one. 'holes' sets the card length when the course has not been mapped; once data/course.json has 'mapped': true the card follows the real hole count and shows par.
_sources: Optional published-CSV overrides. Set 'statusCsv' to a Google Sheet published to the web as CSV and the daily status comes from there instead of data/status.json, which stays as the fallback if the sheet is unreachable. Leave it empty to use the file. See 'The status sheet' in the README for the sheet layout.

homeCourse.name: Home Course
homeCourse.note: STILL A PLACEHOLDER. These are the example course in data/course.json (Pebble Beach), so the weather card matches the layout on the Yardage tab while the club's own course is unmapped. Set them to the real course coordinates — they drive the weather forecast, and until they change it is forecasting the wrong coastline.
homeCourse._forecastUrl: Where the weather card's 'Full forecast and radar' link points. Leave empty to build a Windy link from the coordinates above, which works anywhere. For a US course, https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=LAT&lon=LON is the National Weather Service page; in Canada use the Environment Canada page for the nearest city.

about: Replace these paragraphs with the club introduction. Who the club is for, what a typical week looks like, what a new member should expect at their first practice.
Mention whether beginners are welcome, whether clubs are provided, and what it costs.

photos.caption: Add photos here once Blair has shot some on a clear day. The card hides itself while every 'src' is empty.
